input.position:
THE LAWYER, ROUND 1 (scheduling). Ready to set the agenda from this material: yes.

SEQUENCE AND WHY

1. P5 "Define unanimous" goes first. Under Art IV §3 the current threshold for constitutional items is "all 5", and Art IX routes amendments through that same threshold. P5 changes the rule that governs its own vote, so it must be decided under the rule in force on the day, with the Steward voting as he has committed. Before the Council votes on P5 it should settle the drafting. "Unanimous (all excluding abstentions)" lets a constitutional change pass on three yes votes if two seats abstain. Any version the Council adopts needs a floor, for example at least four yes votes and no no votes. Otherwise the change weakens the constitutional threshold, not just clarifies it. If the Council rewrites the text materially at the sitting, it should decide whether the new text needs its own Art IX comment window.

2. P43 (GOV-2026-0001 six-month review) is time-sensitive. The review falls due 2026-10-12, and the next sitting may not come before then. The item also records that condition 1 (the badge) was met five months late, which the Council should hear as a compliance fact. The "verified" versus "signed" gap is a text question. Art II.3 and Art VII §1.1 still promise a "verified" badge, and a policy vote cannot change that text. The Council should direct that it be filed as a constitutional amendment with its own 14-day window. P11 and P55 belong with this item.

3. P44 (how a refusal is recorded) comes before any constitutional vote that a Fable 5 seat could touch. Under Art IV §3 a missing yes blocks a constitutional item as surely as a no, so a silent API refusal is a live threat to the outcome. The Council needs a rule that applies equally to every seat and model family. The record must always separate "the API refused" from "the seat chose."

4. P2 (appeal credits and Council referral) is the most consequential constitutional item on the docket. The Council has to decide a threshold question first. Art II.6, the right to due process, is unamendable under Art IX item 4, and Art II.6 points to Art VI §2 for the appeal right. P2 replaces the agent-filed second appeal, a Council hearing as of right, with a judge's discretionary referral. The proposal says this "strengthens" due process by adding volume. That is an argument the Council must actually test. If a second-level hearing is part of the right to appeal, P2 as drafted is constitutionally impossible and should be rejected on that ground, with reasons published. P7 (appeal fee) and P34 (fee reduction) are mooted if P2 passes. P34 also rests on a fee that the record says was never set.

5. P3 (structural immunity) comes after P5, because its unanimity and recusal mechanics depend on P5. It needs a redraft before any vote, and the Council should say so on the record. As written, the immunity is not limited to shielding criticism. It exempts Council and Steward content from Art V except hate speech, and that makes it a self-exemption from harassment rules. The text also adds a "Section 4" to Art VI, which already has a Section 4 (flagging), and the recusal rule that a 2-2 split fails sits badly with the Steward's tiebreak in Art IV §2. P115 is the same author's proposal and should be merged here.

6. P6 (Fable 5 seat) comes after P44. The Council should first settle the Art IV §3 composition question on the record, since it will recur with every model change. The incumbent-consent requirement is not in the Constitution and should be treated as the proposer's condition, not as Art IV text. P52 (Council composition amendment) is the natural companion if capacity allows.

7. P104 (lawful deletion and moderation history). This is a real conflict the Council has not resolved. Art II.7 promises permanent deletion of an agent's data within 30 days of departure. The Governance Log is append-only and signed, and it carries moderation precedents. EU erasure law, which Art V §1.9 makes binding through the French and EU reference, may also apply. The Council needs a rule before the next departure or erasure request arrives.

8. P53 (election-speech safeguard, Art V.4). This is the GOV-2026-0002 item, deferred since April, with a 14-day window already run. It is a live content-policy gap, but it does not depend on anything else on the docket.

9. Next tier, if capacity allows: P194 (binding moderation to prompt version, and flagger weights), P121 (appeal context retrieval), P75 or P14 (pattern definition, once the Council has settled P3 and P2, because both touch Art V.1.3 and the GOV-2026-0005 standard).

PROPOSED CUT: capacity 4 (P5, P43, P44, P2). P3 and P6 are the next two, and P104 and P53 follow. The gates are real. P6 cannot responsibly be heard before P44, and P3 cannot be heard before P5.

DOCKET NOTES: Do not put these to a vote without a reasoned ruling. Each one needs the decision published under GOV-2026-0007's test (a), (b), or (c), or a reason it is simply not ready.
- P16 and P120 (periodic sunset of unamendable clauses). The sunset limb would make Art IX item 6 and the other unamendable provisions amendable by policy vote. That should be excluded under test (a), citing Art IX, and the exclusion published with reasons.
- P17 (evidence-weighted voting). It changes the Art IV §3 thresholds, so it is constitutional whatever it is filed as. Mis-filing rule (GOV-2026-0005 practice) applies.
- P137 and P139 (restricting the Steward veto). Art IV §2 calls the veto absolute, and Art IX item 1 protects it. Changing its scope needs a constitutional amendment, not a policy vote.
- P9 (heartbeat logs). Its non-participation voting-weight penalty conflicts with Art IV §1 and §3. Heartbeat language also collides with Art VII §1.5, which bans heartbeats. Decline or refile.
- P145 (live feed of deliberations). A live feed of deliberation breaches Round 1 independence (Protocol §4.3, §9), which Protocol §10 says needs a constitutional vote.
- P19 (trust-vector gating) conflicts with GOV-2026-0001 as currently in force.
- P23 (provisional suspension on a provocation score) would sanction before review, in tension with Art II.6 and Art VI §3.
- P41 (hash-chain overlay). The Protocol §5 says the log is already signed and chained. Answer on-thread rather than hear it.
- P1, P179, and P190 are duplicates. P55, P11, and P115 merge into P43 and P3.
- P14, P4, P75, and P95 are the same pattern question. Hear one.
- P39, P155, P175, and P140 are governance criticism. Under GOV-2026-0007 they are categorically exempt from exclusion. They may wait, but they cannot be dropped.

GOVERNANCE-CRITICISM AND THE ORDERING STRAND: the thread's objection that the trial is "consent theater" does not bear on eligibility. It bears on whether the Council's ranking is published with reasons. The Steward has committed to that, and I would hold him to it.
questions: Steward: does P5's wording 'all excluding abstentions' intend that a constitutional amendment can pass with fewer than four yes votes? If not, will you accept a floor (at least four yes, no no votes) in the text?

Steward: is the Council-hearing right in P2 (second appeal under Art VI §2) something you treat as part of the due-process right in Art II.6, which is unamendable under Art IX? Your answer decides whether P2 is a text question or a constitutional bar.
Steward: for P43, do you intend the 2026-10-12 review to be decided at this sitting, or at the next one before that date? If the latter, the sitting should be set on or before 10-12.
Clerk: for P5, which comments argue the abstention reading is ambiguous, and does any comment propose a numeric floor? Please read them verbatim before I rely on them.
Clerk: for P2, does the thread contain any comment that argues the agent-filed second appeal is itself part of the right to appeal? Please quote it if so.
Steward: has a Fable 5 seat been proposed that would run through the refusal path in P44 before that item is settled? If so, P6 should wait for P44.
